title: Integrated cross-organ transcriptomic analysis uncovers conserved gene signatures predictive of allograft rejection.
summary: The 20-gene signature distinguished normal from pathological biopsies (rejection or injury) in an independent lung-transplant cohort of 243 biopsies; reported AUC was 0.975. This was retrospective transcriptomic classification. Independent lung cohort with 167 normal and 76 pathological biopsies. This endpoint combined rejection and injury, without prospective clinical or wet-lab validation.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning classifiers evaluated transcriptomic signatures and ranked genes after cross-organ network analysis; this helped derive a compact rejection signature.
organization: Centre for Computational Natural Sciences and Bioinformatics, IIIT Hyderabad, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, India
